rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing description combines overwhelming royal power and generosity: God humiliates enemies and honors allies, as his control of the afterlife parallels his treatment of people in worldly history.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك للإعلام بأن تصريفه سبحانه لأحوال الآخرة كما قصد في هذه السورة من تصريفه في أحوال الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence after al-Najm recalls the Prophet’s ascent through the heavens and intimate audience with God, while al-Tur had already signaled his rank; this distinguishes his stature, leaving only sincere believers, while others are obstinate unbelievers.
rows.anchor: جاءت عقب النجم التي شرح فيها الإسراء وكان للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من العظمة بخرق العوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threefold sequence intensifies the warning; the divine name is then prominent in al-Hadid and concludes every verse of al-Mujadilah, deterring disobedience and inviting obedience.
rows.anchor: وكأنها جعلت ثلاثا لإرادة غاية التأكيد لهذا المعنى الشديد , فلما انقضت الثلاثة كان متبركا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman aims to establish God’s universal mercy, shown by his knowledge and power in creation’s wonders, recalling blessings to encourage gratitude and warn of the loss of further favor through vengeance.
rows.anchor: مقصودها بالذات إثبات الاتصاف بعموم الرحمة ترغيبا في إنعامه وإحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title ‘Bride of the Qur’an’ says the surah gathers the Qur’an’s adornments, beauties, jewels, and crowns.
rows.anchor: واسمها عروس القرآن واضح البيان في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, Allah’s name points to the encompassing perfection made visible in the marvels of creation.
rows.anchor: الذي ظهرت إحاطة كماله بما ظهر من عجائب مخلوقاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, al-Rahman’s universal mercy appears through the wonders of creation and signs.
rows.anchor: الذي ظهر عموم رحمته بما بهر من بدائع مصنوعاته واشتهر من عظيم آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, al-Rahim singles out the obedient, whose humility through worship brings them honor and God’s approval.
rows.anchor: الذي ظهر اختصتصه لأهل طاعته بما تحققوا به من الذل المفيد للعز بلزوم عباداته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pearl is exceptionally white, bright, and pure; coral is the red branches, differing from pearl in color and use.
rows.anchor: وهو الدر الذي هو في غاية البياض والإشراق والصفاء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, as transmitted by Ibn Atiyya, identifies pearl as white and coral as red branches; Ibn Atiyya calls this the familiar usage.
rows.anchor: نقل هذا القول ابن عطية عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: جمع كثير
rows.claim: Many commentators instead say that pearl means large pearls and coral means small pearls.
rows.anchor: وقال جمع كثير : إن اللؤلؤ كبار الدر والمرجان صغاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain challenges the jinn and humans to deny the great marine blessings, including sight from above and the useful things created in the seas and made available to them.
rows.anchor: أبنعمة البصر من جهة الفوق أو غير ذلك من خلق المنافع في البحار وتسليطكم عليها وإخراج الحلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting ‘to Him’ stresses that ships belong to God; apparent human control is negligible, so people must not credit visible causes or adopt the views of those who say union or oneness.
rows.anchor: وأشار بتقديم الجار إلى أن السائر في الفلك لا تصريف له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘running ones’ are ships of every size, whether empty or carrying cargo.
rows.anchor: أي السفن الكبار والصغار الفارغة والمشحونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is related to rising or growing; the sails rise, and the ships set out on their course.
rows.anchor: من نشأ - إذا وربا , والسحابة : ارتفعت , وأصل الناشئ

rows.speaker: حمزة وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Hamzah and Abu Bakr read the shīn with kasra: the ships raise their sails and initiate sailing; the other readers’ fatḥa makes them ships constructed, launched, and given raised sails by their maker.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قراءة حمزة وأبي بكر بكسر الشين أنها رافعة شراعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships resemble tall mountains, though they float high on the water while also remaining submerged in it.
rows.anchor: مع كونها عالية على الماء منغمسة فيه مع أنه ليس لها من نفسها إلا الرسوب والغوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shipbuilding, sailing, fishing, trade over great distances, rescue in storms, and guidance in making ships are further favors; divine direction makes their use possible.
rows.anchor: من المنافع بالتكسب من البحر بالصيد وغيره والتوصل إلى البلاد الشاسعة للفوائد الهائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships and their crews illustrate the ordered kingdom: ships serve like angels, passengers resemble accountable creatures carried from exile toward home, and their commander issues orders from above.
rows.anchor: فخدامها كالملائكة في إقامة الملكوت وتحسين تماسكه بإذن ربهم

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barrajān reads the ship inwardly as worldly life: the body is its vessel, the inner self its passenger, reason its captain, faculties its crew, faith its provisions, success its wind, remembrance its sail, and the Messenger its pilot.
rows.anchor: فالدنيا هي البحر , والسفينة جسمه , وباطن العبد هو المحمول فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything on earth—including both land and sea—and even the heavens will perish; all besides God is contingent, existing between nonexistence before creation and nonexistence after extinction.
rows.anchor: أي هالك ومعدوم بالفعل بعد أن كان هو وغيره من سائر ما سوى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creatures undergo continual making and unmaking in their states, qualities, and powers, while causes of destruction surround them unseen, as they do passengers in a ship.
rows.anchor: ثم هو فيما بين ذلك يتعاوره الإيجاد والإفناء في حين من أحواله وأعراضه وقواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face is the noblest part of a being and can stand for its possessor; since it cannot remain apart from its possessor, it conveys the continued existence of the whole after creation perishes.
rows.anchor: الوجه أشرف ما في الوجود , وكان بعر به عما أريد به صاحب الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God remains forever after all else perishes. ‘Your Lord’s face’ refers to his essence, the noblest aspect of his being; the wording is more eloquent than ‘its possessor.’
rows.anchor: أي بعد فناء الكل , بقاء مستمرا إلى ما لا نهاية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord is the one who nurtures the Prophet through the message and revelation toward boundless knowledge; seeking his face also means acting sincerely for God.
rows.anchor: أي المربي لك بالرسالة والترقية بهذا الوحي إلى ما لا يحد من المعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religious principle that nothing resembles God prevents a corporeal reading of ‘face’; God is free of need and deficiency, unlike all observable creatures.
rows.anchor: وكان من المقرر عند أهل الشرع أنه سبحانه ليس كمثله شيء فلا يتوهم أحد منهم من التعبير به نقصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Possessor of majesty’ describes God’s essence: unsurpassable greatness that excludes everything unworthy of him.
rows.anchor: أي العظمة التي لا ترام وهو صفة ذاته التي تقتضي إجلاله عن كل ما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘And honor’ describes God’s action, his general beneficence.
rows.anchor: أي الإحسان العام وهو صفة فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death itself brings blessings, including succession in which one person’s death benefits others; the refrain also points to hearing and the creation, extinction, and inheritance of creatures.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الموت نفسه فيه نعم لا تنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Need indicates contingency and divine independence indicates eternal being; every creature in the heavens and earth continually asks God by its state, speech, or both.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أدل دليل على العدم الحاجة , وعلى دوام الوجود الغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Day’ here stands for any moment, the smallest bounded span of perceptible time; God is continuously engaged in affairs.
rows.anchor: عبر به عن أقل الزمان كما عبر به عن أخف الموزونات بالذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women resemble ruby in smoothness and translucence and coral in whiteness and beauty.
rows.anchor: في بياضه , وصغار الدر أنصع بياضا

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus says the finest ruby is pomegranate-red and is useful for obsessive thoughts, palpitations, and weak heart when drunk, and for blood stagnation when worn.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس : أجوده الأحمر الرماني نافع للوسواس والخفقان وضعف القلب شربا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz identifies coral with small pearls; the source adds that a red marine growth is also known as coral.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله القزاز : والمرجان صغار اللؤلؤ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their color does not change; this is consistent with the report that the marrow of a woman’s leg can be seen through seventy garments.
rows.anchor: ألوانهن وهو مع ذلك صابت لا يعتريه تغير ليطابق الحديث الذي فيه ( يرى مخ ساقها من وراء سبعين حلة )

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan limits the comparison to the traits that suit it: ruby’s smoothness and translucence, and coral’s smoothness and lovely appearance.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : شبههن بهما فيما يحسن التشبيه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their beauty exceeds what one object could represent, so God combines two transparent objects as comparisons; a cited line likewise compares a woman’s contrasting colors to silver mixed with gold.
rows.anchor: من تشبيه شيء بشيئين لبلوغ الأمر في الحسن إلى حد لا يساويه فيه شيء واحد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet explaining that God asks whether the reward for one whom he blessed with monotheism is anything but Paradise; the servant’s good work is rewarded in return for God’s nurturing favor. No grading is given.
rows.anchor: روى البغوي بسنده عن أنس رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states that good deeds by humans, jinn, or others receive good reward; repeating the familiar definite term gives it a different meaning, and the passage closes eight exhortations toward the eight gates of the garden of the near ones.
rows.anchor: فهذا من المواضع التي أعيدت فيها المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two gardens lie below the first pair in place and rank and are for the lower-ranking, God-fearing people of the right hand, beneath the gardens of the foremost doers of good.
rows.anchor: أي من أدنى مكان , رتبة مما تحت جنتي هؤلاء المحسنين المقربين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas understands ‘below them’ to mean lower in degree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : دونهما في الدرج

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barrajān distributes the four gardens between the two groups and sees their number as alluding to the four seasons; he interprets the gold and silver gardens report accordingly.
rows.anchor: وجعل ابن برجان الأربع موزعة بين الكل , وأن تخصيص هذه العدة

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barrajān also allows ‘below’ to mean nearer to human beings, identifying these gardens with the intermediate realm and its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: ثم جوز أن يكون المراد بالدون الأدنى إلى الإنسان , وهو البرزخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two gardens are intensely green, their lushness darkening toward black because of abundant moisture; the word derives from ‘darkness.’
rows.anchor: أي خضراوان خضرة تضرب من شدة الري إلى السواد , من الدهمة

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani says these gardens are dominated by ground-covering plants and herbs, unlike the earlier pair, which has trees and fruit.
rows.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : الغالب على هاتين الجنتين النبات والرياحين المنبسطة على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could make the water bitter and briny when it descends or before people use it; this is more likely than crops becoming dry, so the conditional is not emphatic, as listeners already recognize his power.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت صيرورة الماء ملحا أكثر من صيرورة النبت حطاما , ولم يؤكد لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should continually thank God by using the powers he supplied in obedience, since he made the water pleasant and useful to them.
rows.anchor: فهل لا ولم لا تجددون الشكر على سبيل الاستمرار باستعمال ما أفادكم ذلك من القوى في طاعة الذي أوجده لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks people to inspect with eyes and insight the particular fire they kindle, so they recognize God’s power through an unexpected created sign.
rows.anchor: أي أخبروني هل رأيتم بالأبصار والبصائر ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is struck from a firestick, whether dry or green; it is hidden in the wood until extracted, surprising anyone who has not tried it.
rows.anchor: أي تستخرجون من الزند فتوقودون به سواء كان الزند يابسا أو أخضر بعد أن كانت خفية فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden fire’s emergence evokes tawriya, where one thing appears while another is intended; the concealed flame then manifests with great power.
rows.anchor: فكان ذلك مثل التورية التي يظهر فيها شيء ويراد غيره , ثم صار بعد ذلك الخفاء إلى ظهور عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire exists in every tree, but people use markh and afar because they kindle especially easily; a cited saying says fire is in every tree, but these two are best.
rows.anchor: في كل شجر نار واستمجد المرخ والعفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since producing fire from wood is a wonder, God repeats the question and denial to draw attention to it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا من عجائب الصنع , كرر التقرير والإنكار تنبيها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb asks whether people originated, implanted, revived, cultivated, and caused the firewood tree to grow.
rows.anchor: أي اخترعتم وأوجدتم وأودعتم وأحييتم وربيتم وأوقعتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree means markh and afar, whose branches are used as firesticks.
rows.anchor: أي المرخ والعفار التي تتخذون منها الزناد الذي يخرج منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People do not create the tree or embed fire in it; God places fire in green wood mixed with its opposite, water, without either overcoming the other.
rows.anchor: أسكنتموها النار مختلطة بالماء الذي هو ضدها وخبأتموها في تلك الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God brings the tree into this form and creates its hidden fire, underscoring his exclusive creative power.
rows.anchor: أي لها بما لنا من العظمة على تلك الهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating fire in fresh, water-bearing wood proves God can restore softness and life to dry, decomposed bodily dust at resurrection.
rows.anchor: فمن قدر على إيجاد النار التي هي أيبس ما يكون من الشجرة الأخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses paired ellipsis (iḥtibāk), as do its sister verses.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك بمثل ما مضى في أخوتها سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic ‘We’ means God alone made the fire a reminder of resurrection, the punishment of the greater Fire, the tree of Zaqqūm, and other realities revealed to the perceptive.
rows.anchor: بما اقتضته عظمتنا , وقدم من منافعها ما هو أولى بسياق البعث

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barrajān compares striking fire from wood to the cry among people and to God’s creation of bodies from the unseen; the greater Fire lies hidden beyond the visible world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : فوزان قدح الزناد من الشجر , والزناد وزان الصيحة بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made fire a constant reminder of what people light with it, making reflection and admonition more likely.
rows.anchor: وعلق بحا سبحانه كثيرا من أسباب المعاش التي لا غنى عنها ليكون مذكرا لهم بما أوقدوا به حاضرا دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire is a lasting, indispensable means for livelihood and reaching one’s aims, providing light, warmth, cooking, processing, melting, hardening, and protection from predators.
rows.anchor: أي إنشاء وبقاء وتعميرا ونفعا وإيصالا إلى غاية المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘For the hungry’ refers to empty bellies; it also refers to those who arrive in barren, remote wilderness, and anyone suited to such a wasteland can bear the description even when elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي الجياع الذي أقوت بطونهم - أي خلت -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qiwāʾ is a barren wilderness, far from habitation, broad, empty, and remote.
rows.anchor: والقواء بالكسر والمد أي القفر الخالية المتباعدة الأطراف البعيدة من العمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mujadilah warns that God will inflict severe punishment on those who oppose him and his Messenger; complete knowledge entails complete power and encompasses every perfection.
rows.anchor: بمن حاد الله ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما له سبحانه من تمام العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title refers to the opening story and the surah’s ending; the repeated comprehensive divine name throughout the story and every verse is unusually pervasive.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك دلت تسميتها بالمجادلة بأول قصتها وآخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated divine names present believers who have erred or disobeyed under both majesty and perfection, showing that both descriptions apply to them.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن الأكثر منها المراد فيها بالخطاب من يصح أن ينظر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah strongly condemns certain acts when believers commit them and does not legalize them to satisfy natural desire; the author contrasts them with eating and intercourse permitted on Ramadan nights.
rows.anchor: شدد النكير فيها حين وقع بعض أهل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading supports the author’s earlier account of why al-Waqiʿah, al-Rahman, and al-Qamar lack the comprehensive divine name repeated in al-Mujadilah.
rows.anchor: وهذا مؤيد لما تقدم من سر إخلاء الواقعة والرحمن والقمر من هذا الاسم الجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, Allah’s encompassing knowledge completes his power and attributes; al-Rahman gives generously by creating all and sending guides, while al-Rahim singles out his chosen with the favor of divine approval.
rows.anchor: الذي أحاط علمه فتمت قدرته فكملت جميع صفاته
